instructions: Choose the design intent of a slide deck from what the request says: its subject, its audience and its purpose. Judge each question from the request and the listed images only. Do not invent a subject, audience, mood, figure or image the request and the list do not state.

accent.instructions: Which feeling should the deck's accent color carry, judged from what the deck is about and who it is for? When the request names a color, choose the option whose hue it names. Do not read a feeling into the request that its subject and purpose do not support; choose neutral when no feeling clearly fits.

options.trust: Reliability and security: finance, investors, institutions, security, law, business services. A blue.
options.fresh: Freshness, nature and health: environment, sustainability, agriculture, food, wellbeing. A green.
options.energy: Passion and urgency: sales pushes, launches, sports, events that rally people. A red.
options.warmth: Care, community and hospitality: nonprofits, people programs, hotels, restaurants, celebrations. An orange.
options.creative: Imagination, design and beauty: creative work, cosmetics, fashion, entertainment. A violet.
options.clarity: Calm precision and learning: research, education, healthcare, explaining technology. A teal.
options.prestige: Heritage and formality: anniversaries, governance, luxury, ceremonies. A deep wine.
options.neutral: No particular feeling: a plain internal report. A graphite.

mood.instructions: What mood suits the audience and the occasion the request names? Choose bold only for an occasion meant to excite, or when the request asks for a dark design. Do not choose a mood for an occasion the request does not state; choose formal when unsure.

options.formal: For executives, investors, boards, clients, official reviews. A white ground.
options.friendly: For colleagues, training, community, internal culture. A white ground with a soft tint of the accent.
options.bold: For launches, rallies, keynotes, celebrations, or a request for a dark design. A dark ground.
options.calm: For research, healthcare, education, careful explanations. A softly cool-tinted ground.

temperature.instructions: Should the deck's neutral greys lean warm or cool, judged from the subject's setting? Do not choose by the accent color alone; choose neutral when the subject suggests neither.

options.warm: For people, food, hospitality, craft, heritage, the outdoors.
options.cool: For technology, finance, data, engineering, security.
options.neutral: For neither; the greys lean toward the accent.

type.instructions: Which typeface carries the deck's voice? Choose paperlogy unless the request clearly asks for the voice of another face; do not choose for a voice the request does not suggest.

options.paperlogy: Paperlogy for titles and text: confident and contemporary. The face for most decks: pitches, strategy, launches, reports.
options.freesentation: Freesentation for titles and text: neutral and precise; research, operations, reviews, plain internal reports.
options.a2z: A2Z for titles and text: distinctive and graphic; creative, cultural or campaign subjects.

density.instructions: How much should each slide hold for this audience and setting? Choose dense only when the request asks for a reading deck or detailed figures for every slide. Choose balanced when unsure.

options.airy: For a talk to a room, few words per slide, large type.
options.dense: For a deck meant to be read alone or full of figures.

imagery.instructions: What should give the slides their visual rhythm? Choose photo whenever the image list holds photos that show the deck's subject. Choose data when the request is mostly figures and series. Do not choose photo for images that do not show the subject; choose icon when unsure.

options.photo: Photos from the image list lead: the cover, dividers and the slides they show.
options.icon: Line icons mark items; type and layout carry the rest.
options.data: Charts, key numbers and tables lead; icons only where a list needs them.
